description: Two-channel counterpoint sequencer: each of four stages carries a slider for channel A and one for channel B, and a trigger flips which of the two that stage feeds

params.text: Adds its setting to the A output while that stage is flipped to channel A, 0V fully down to 1.25V fully up, or 2V with the wider range chosen for channel A
Adds its setting to the B output while that stage is flipped to channel B, 0V fully down to 1.25V fully up, or 2V with the wider range chosen for channel B

inputs.text: Flips all four stages away from channel A on a rising edge above 2V, leaving the A output at 0V and the B output carrying all four of its sliders
Flips all four stages away from channel B on a rising edge above 2V, leaving the B output at 0V and the A output carrying all four of its sliders
Flips the first stage between channel A and channel B on each rising edge above 2V
Flips that stage between channel A and channel B on each rising edge above 2V; with no cable in it, the stage is flipped by every second trigger of the stage before it

outputs.text: The sum of the A sliders of whichever stages are flipped to channel A, so 0V to 5V, or 0V to 8V with the wider range chosen for channel A
The sum of the B sliders of whichever stages are flipped to channel B, so 0V to 5V, or 0V to 8V with the wider range chosen for channel B

notes: every stage comes up flipped to channel B, so the A output starts at 0V and the B output carries all four of its sliders
a stage feeds one channel or the other and never both, so the two outputs together always carry the same set of four stages divided between them
the lamp in a slider lights while that stage is feeding that channel, and the two lamps by the outputs brighten with the voltage each output is carrying
on a sample where either reset jack fires, the stage triggers are not read at all, so a trigger arriving at the same moment as a reset is lost
menu: 2V range for channel A — makes each of channel A's four sliders span 0V to 2V in place of 0V to 1.25V, so the A output reaches 8V
2V range for channel B — makes each of channel B's four sliders span 0V to 2V in place of 0V to 1.25V, so the B output reaches 8V
